hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary:
Three records carry the design, and both paths into the analyzer use them: the lookup pipeline that serves the agent tools and builds every run context, and the plan tree above it that serves broad analyses. The plan tree does not run today for a request that asks no specific question, so two Stories first make such a request run and then make a broad analysis complete; the other Stories apply to both paths once it does. A completeness record on every lookup result and every plan-task result replaces today's mix of truncated flags, totals, free-text notes and log lines: it says whether the result is complete, how many items exist and were returned, why any are missing, what was skipped or only partly read, and what the result rests on (text on disk, the stored graph, the document index, a live data source). A lookup that cannot run is always the existing failed output with its reason, never an empty result, and a failure to write the answer is reported with what was found, not passed silently to another way of answering. An answer report heads every answer on both paths: one overall completeness statement derived from those records, the measured size, and how the request was handled.

A request measure says what a request touches and maps it to the existing five sizes. It has two sources, because the size is needed at two different moments. A request that plans lookups up front is measured from what those lookups returned. A request that plans none up front (an unfocused request on the plan-tree path, where the size is needed before planning) is measured from the area it names: the files and entities the graph store holds under the path or repo it points at. No size is taken from the wording or assumed; a request that cannot be measured is treated as the largest size and says so.

Handling is a stated table from size to method, on both paths. Up to the size a model can reason over together, the answer is written in one pass, as today. Above it, the results are divided into parts along file and directory boundaries, each part is reasoned over in turn, and a combine step joins the per-part results into one answer; a failed part is kept out and named in the report. A single item too large for one pass is read in consecutive sections under the same rule. Once that handling exists the limits are removed: no lookup, plan-task runtime, planning prompt or text search keeps a limit on how many results it returns or how much of an item it reads. Last, layouts are selected by question kind and source kind together; a new question kind, enumeration, is rendered directly from lookup results with no model in the path, and the layouts lose their limits and describe every lookup they may draw on.

ownedContracts.name: Handling report
ownedContracts.purpose: How a request was handled: at once or in parts, how many parts, and which parts were not covered.

consumedContracts.name: Completeness record
consumedContracts.purpose: The one statement every lookup result and every plan-task result carries about whether it is complete; also the rule that a lookup which cannot run is the failed output, never an empty result. The existing failed output is kept for a lookup that could not run, and gains one optional field for what was found before it failed.

consumedContracts.name: Answer report
consumedContracts.purpose: The header every answer carries on both paths: overall completeness derived from the results, then the measured size and how the request was handled once those exist. Owned by the first Story so that sizing, handling and layout each fill and render their part.

consumedContracts.name: Request measure
consumedContracts.purpose: What a request actually touched, from its lookup results or from the area it names, and the size it maps to.

consumedContracts.name: Causes of not proceeding
consumedContracts.purpose: What a request that cannot proceed reports. Three codes are added, all declared by Story s6, to the plan tree's existing list (RunErrorCode) and to the daemon's error codes (AnalyzeRpcErrorCode); its failure type (RunFailure) and its stages (RunStage) are kept as they are, and 'shaper-llm-unavailable' is kept for a model call that failed. A kind of scope that does not go with a kind of source keeps the existing code 'scope-ref-kind-target-mismatch'.

boundary.internal: The table from size to handling method and the size above which results are handled in parts. How outputs are divided along directory and file boundaries, and one large item into consecutive sections, so that a single item is read in full. In the lookup pipeline: writing a per-part result for each part serially and the new combine step (its input, its output, its own size rule, its failure case). On the plan tree: the same size rule on the aggregator's input, combining in stages. Keeping a failed part out of the combined answer. The step tool's part turn. Filling the handling report and showing it in the answer. The limits are still in place, so this is exercised by results that are large within them and by tests that lower the threshold. This Story closes the exception accepted on Story s7: a broad docs analysis whose aggregate input is larger than one model call accepts must complete once that input is handled in parts.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: With every limit still in place: returning the completeness record from each lookup and each plan-task runtime, saying when a limit was reached (limited), what was skipped and what was only partly read, and the basis each rests on. For the text search, reporting what it leaves out today: files over its size limit, files it could not read, lines it shortened, output it discarded, and the files each backend excludes by rule. Classifying every catch clause in the lookups and the plan-task runtimes: a clause that handles a named, expected condition stays and names what it skipped in the record; a clause that swallows an error is removed or rethrows, so that the lookup becomes the failed output. Deriving the answer report's overall completeness from those records and writing the completeness line at the head of every answer on both paths, in the layouts as they are today. Reporting a failure of the answer-writing step as a typed error that carries the lookup results and the report, in place of the 'model unavailable' error that discards them today, added as one more case to the raise site and the mapping that Story s6 owns, and passed through everything that reaches the context builder (six callers, the one-shot agent tool and the daemon's workflow runner, with the error's data carried through the daemon's error mapping). Keeping the report out of the schema given to a model at both places the schema reaches one (the answer-writing call and the tool loop's final answer), and rejecting a report an agent supplies. What the step tool attaches to a bundle the agent wrote. The declared report field on the bundle, its schema version, and how bundles and run records stored before the change are treated. The lookup cache's version. The lookup cache's stored shape changes with the outputs. The free-form fallback: an optional field for partial findings on the failed output, the loop's exit at the limit attaching what it gathered, reaching its turn limit becoming a failed output, and its answer gets a report that says it rests on a search directed by a model. Reading the data drivers' cut flag into the completeness record of the table-listing lookup and the object-listing plan task.

The two measuring sources and the mapping from counts to the five sizes. From lookup results, at all four places that assume a size today. From the named area, on the plan tree: the measuring pass after both classification branches, removal of the scope picker's model call, removal of the size from the classifier's output, what the decomposer and planner receive as size at each moment, the size's effect on plan depth as well as task count, and measuring a child plan from the area it names when it is spawned, with the planner model's figure and a size on the daemon request kept as hints. A size given by a caller or a slash command kept as a hint. The unmeasurable case. Filling the measure into the answer report and showing it in the answer. The source of the measure for each of the seven kinds of scope, including counting a data connection's tables or objects from the live source through the data driver, and the fallback to XL, recorded as not determined, when a count cannot be taken. Adding a complete mode to the data drivers' listings for the count (the five relational drivers, four of the six namespace drivers, the file listing; Redis and etcd are recorded as not determined, since their listing is a sample of keys), with the limited mode kept for other callers; a listing that reports it was cut is never a determined count.

Removing every limit on how many results a lookup or plan-task runtime returns: the sixteen sites the Define lists and those found since, in the lookups (the maxSources parameter of the two document lookups, the result cut in document retrieval, the cuts inside capability reuse-check, table describe and the document family summary, the preview limits of doc.mention) and in the plan-task runtimes (the file-list and file caps of data and infrastructure discovery and their sample caps). Removing the fixed cuts on an item's content at nine sites: the eight found when the Epic was defined, including the three adherence checks, and the indexer's own cut of a stored body to 8,192 characters (src/indexer/parser/artifact.ts), which Story s1 reports with the item's real length. The index is a pointer: at each of the nine sites, where an item's content matters to the answer, the analyzer reads the item from its file at the place the index points to and does not rely on the body the index stores. What the index stores and how it is built are not changed. The complete mode of the text search for both backends: no limit on hits, no per-file match limit, no cut of a matching line, no skipping of a file for its size, no discarding of output (the search's output is read as a stream, not kept up to a fixed size), a stated rule for a search that runs out of time (reported as failed, never as complete), and the files each backend excludes by rule stated in the result. Removing the limit parameters, their examples and the fan-out bound from the planning prompt. What was reported as limited in Story s1 now does not occur; the larger results are handled by Story s3's method. Raising the lookup cache's version again, and dropping limit parameters before a lookup's cache key is taken. Building cancellation (a signal from each caller through the context builder to a check between turns; the run's signal into the plan walk and the classifier; the optional signal on the daemon's standard handlers; the signal parameter on the daemon's context-building functions; a signal on the step tool's plan and narrow phases, through stepPlan and the runner context; the new cancel request for the five requests received over the socket that reach a tool loop (the three context requests, the plan request and the classify request), with the daemon's table of run id to canceller; the cancelled case in the classify stage's mapping; 'aborted' in the daemon's error codes; what a cancelled loop returns), moving the table-listing lookup and the object-listing plan task to the complete mode of the data drivers' listings, and only then removing the turn limit and retiring its configuration setting (catalog row, retired list, the analyzer's configuration, the planning prompt, the VS Code extension's declaration with a release, the pages that document it, the reconcile fixture) for all three users of the loop (the free-form lookup and the classification and task modes) and giving the loop the complete mode of its search tools. Removing the error and the code for reaching the turn limit from both lists and both mappings, with the tests that import the error and the test configuration that sets the limit.

Adding the enumeration question kind to the planner's choices and rendering it directly from lookup results, including returning it from the step tool's plan phase with no model turn. Choosing a layout by question kind and source kind at both places a layout is selected today. Removing the limits from the six layouts and the older per-source layouts and from the summariser's output schema. Making each layout describe every lookup it may draw on, with that reference at the end of the prompt. Laying out the answer report, which Stories s1 to s3 already write, in the form each layout uses.

Giving a request that asks no specific question a run context: what the lookup pipeline plans for it (a broad survey of the area it names, from the lookups that exist) where today it returns at once; the same for a request started with a stated kind of source, which is always marked unfocused; serving, in the lookup pipeline, the four kinds of scope it returns for today (a file, a symbol, a manifest directory, a data connection), and how each resolves to what the lookups need. Replacing the single 'model unavailable' error with the cause of each way of not proceeding, as new codes in the existing list and new typed errors, and with the existing codes where one fits: every place the pipeline returns nothing, and the fall-through for a bundle that fails validation, is listed and given its cause. It owns the place the error is raised, the pipeline's rule for returning nothing, and the functions that map these errors to codes (the plan tree's and the daemon's, and the classify stage's mapping, through which an error from the classifier's context build is routed). The form of a symbol scope's value, its resolution to one stored entity, and the validator and classifier prompt brought in line. The one function that resolves a scope's value to a repo, a path or an entity, and moving the lookup pipeline's direct readers of the value to it (the planning prompt, the context builder's path resolution, the indexed check). Correcting the table of which kind of scope goes with which kind of source, with the classifier prompt's copy of it, the table's comment and the matrix test, and applying it on both classification branches: the plan tree's classify mapping surfaces the validator's inner code, and the branch with no classifier calls the validator's checks directly. Supplying the connection check from both callers of the classifier, and mapping a connection id to its repo. It declares all three new codes in both lists; Stories s1 and s7 raise one each.

Widening the plan tasks of each family (code, docs, infra, data) to exactly the kinds of scope the corrected table gives it, with the scope check the docs tasks share with the code tasks taking the family's row as an argument, and every task that reads the scope's value directly (three docs tasks, the shared adherence task, the task that lists data connections) moved to the resolution function Story s6 defines, including a data connection for the data tasks, and refusing any other pairing with the existing code for it. Running a broad analysis through classification, the run context, planning, the plan walk with its nested plans, and the aggregator, to a final report; finding and correcting what stops it at each stage. A stop the run catches is already recorded; what is added is a handler for an error nothing catches, in the plan walk and in the daemon's request, that writes the run record, and the rule that a record still in progress with no live run behind it is abandoned: the process's in-memory count of the runs it is executing per id, and the two readers that apply it, the status request and the purge, each rewriting the record as failed with the code 'run-abandoned', which Story s6 declares and this Story raises; a new run replaces a record left in progress with its own first record. Making a task's refusal of a scope a typed error the plan walk recognises, with an optional code on the failed-task record. Its design begins by running one and recording how far it gets; if what is found is more than one Story, it is brought back to be split. Two stops the first runs of 2026-10-08 found are corrected here as well: the aggregate-report task runs on the inputs that exist when a task before it failed and is told which are absent, so that a run with a failed task returns a report that names what is missing; and the daemon's run request accepts an empty prompt when the caller states the kind of source. Two further stops are not this Story's: what the code tasks treat as a module is Story s8's, and an aggregate input larger than one model call accepts is Story s3's. For the second, a broad docs analysis not completing on a repository of that size is an exception the stakeholder accepted on 2026-10-08, to be closed by Story s3.
Private implementation of s8: The code tasks of a broad analysis work on a repository whose graph has no modules for its directories

nonFunctional.performance: A request small enough for one pass makes the same model calls as today, and one fewer on the plan tree, where the model call that picked a size is replaced by a count from the graph store. A request handled in parts makes one call per part plus the combination, serially; that time is accepted because accuracy comes before cost. After the limits are removed, a complete text search over a large repository is the cost of a text lookup.
nonFunctional.observability: Every answer on both paths states its completeness, its measured size and counts, and its handling method and part count; each lookup and plan-task result states its own completeness. A failed lookup, part or answer-writing step carries its reason.
nonFunctional.durability: Cached lookup outputs written before this change lack the completeness record and are treated as absent, not as complete.
nonFunctional.security: No change: lookups stay inside the repository's dependency closure and the existing scope checks on paths remain.

summary.prose: This Story adds one shared helper that divides an answer-writing model call's input into ordered parts when the HLD's table from measured size to method says so, or when the rendered input is not admitted by a provable bound: a CLI provider's declared character budget, or, for a local model, a UTF-8 byte count held under the window minus the call's output tokens minus a template reserve. A single pass keeps the configured output tokens (10,240 bytes with the checked-in configuration); part and combine calls on a local model use a stated lower output cap of 8,192 tokens, enforced by the local provider as its generation limit (22,528 bytes), so the largest existing prompt plus the minimum room fits; a CLI provider enforces no output cap and needs none, because a part reply never enters a later call. On the checked-in local configuration code and adherence requests are always handled in parts, which departs from the wording of ac4 and was accepted by the user on 2026-11-08. The helper owns the schema-repair loop with one provider attempt and provider retries off, measures every repair before it is sent, and classifies each failure by cause (call failed, invalid reply, unadmittable). Each part is reasoned over serially, sections never split a code point, evidence and findings are assembled in code, and a staged combine writes only a bounded summary and always ends, falling back to the per-part results; a successful part is never discarded. Four callers use it; on the ordinary success path the handling and the uncovered parts are applied to the report that is stamped on the delivered bundle; the handling report is typed and shown in the answer's head; and every failure keeps its true reason, cause and data, in a JSON-safe form, through the existing mappings, the free-form executor, the aggregator boundary, the plan walk (nested plans included), the stored task record and the orchestrator.

dataModelChanges.details: The sc4 contract typed. method, parts, partitionedBy, notCovered[{part, reason}] as sketched, plus additive fields: combineStages (optional), budgets (an array of {unit: 'chars' | 'bytes', limit, source: 'provider' | 'context-window' | 'default', basis: 'declared' | 'bytes-bound' | 'default', inputSize}, never mixing units) and trigger (optional: 'size' | 'fit' | 'both'; absent on a single pass). partitionedBy gains 'mixed'. parseHandling accepts a record with or without trigger. Counting: parts is the number of first-level parts including failed ones; a single pass has parts 1. A part id is its ordinal and heading ('part 3: docs/a'); mergeHandling qualifies it with the plan path. Composition by mergeHandling(first, second, prefix): an absent side is ignored; method is 'partitioned' if either is; parts is the sum (a single pass counts 1); notCovered is the concatenation with the first side's part ids qualified by the prefix; budgets is the concatenation de-duplicated on (unit, limit, source, basis), keeping the largest inputSize of identical entries, so a local 'bytes-bound' entry survives a merge with a CLI entry and units are never compared; combineStages is the sum when either has it; partitionedBy is the common value or 'mixed'; trigger is the union when either has one. So a single-pass root with a partitioned child reports 'partitioned' with parts one more than the child's.

dataModelChanges.details: Type changes from unknown to HandlingReport | undefined. Current-behaviour invariant it might break: the bundle schema declares handling as an open object, so a stored value such as {} is valid today, and isAnswerReport does not validate it. A read-boundary guard parseHandling(value: unknown): HandlingReport | undefined accepts only a value with the required fields and treats anything else as absent; mergeHandling, renderReportHead and isAnswerReport use it, and a stored {} is read as no handling.

dataModelChanges.entity: The report on the ordinary success path (found.report)
dataModelChanges.details: In the lookup pipeline the driver derives found.report from the lookups before any answer is written and settlePipelineOutcome passes that report to the stamp callback, which builds the delivered bundle as { ...raw, report, meta } (src/analyze/context/driver.ts around 577 and 1476); the model's own report is never used. Because synthesize returns only the seven layers, a handling report produced while synthesizing would have no path to the delivered bundle, and a successful partial answer would keep complete=true from the lookups. The transition: the driver calls synthesizeHandled, builds found' = { ...found, report: applyHandling(found.report, handling) } and returns it in the 'bundle' outcome; settlePipelineOutcome then hands the updated report to the stamp callback. applyHandling sets handling by mergeHandling, adds one incomplete source note per not-covered part (sourceKind 'lookup', sourceId 'answer step / <part id>') and sets complete false when a part is not covered, including a combine fallback ('combine' in notCovered). A single pass adds the single-pass handling and leaves completeness as it was. The free-form short-circuit applies the same function to the report that reportFromLookups derives, using the handling extractSoleFreeformResult returns. On a thrown answer-step failure the error already carries found, whose report is built from the error's handling by the same function.

dataModelChanges.entity: HANDLING_TABLE, the admission rule and the output caps
dataModelChanges.details: HANDLING_TABLE maps the sc3 size to the method: XS and S single pass, M, L and XL partitioned; an undetermined measure is XL. The size reaches every caller of the helper, the free-form final emit through the tool loop included. The admission rule decides whether a rendered input (messages, repeated context, absent-input section) may be sent, in two units that are never mixed. For a CLI provider: characters, against the declared inputBudgetChars minus a 16,000-character reserve (basis 'declared'). For a local model: the UTF-8 byte length against the window tokens (the figure ollamaContextWindow gives num_ctx) minus the call's output tokens minus 2,048 for template and special tokens (basis 'bytes-bound'), because every token covers at least one byte, so the byte length bounds the token count and an admitted input cannot be truncated. Output tokens are per call kind and apply to a local model only: a single pass keeps the configured ollamaNumPredict; part and combine calls use the constant PART_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 8,192, enough for a seven-layer reply with a summary capped at 2,000 characters, and OllamaProvider enforces it as num_predict (a reply cut at the cap ends mid-JSON and fails validation as an invalid reply). A CLI provider enforces no output cap: CliProvider.modelArgs ignores the completion options and the Vibe path forwards no limit. None is needed for the admission bound: a CLI provider's admission is input characters only, and a part reply's size never enters a later model call, because the combine reads only the part summaries (capped at 2,000 characters by the schema) and the evidence layers are assembled in code from the replies into the delivered answer. Worked with the checked-in configuration (a 32,768-token window and ollamaNumPredict 20,480): single pass 32,768 - 20,480 - 2,048 = 10,240 bytes; part and combine 32,768 - 8,192 - 2,048 = 22,528 bytes. The existing prompts alone are 10,652 bytes (code), 11,040 (adherence) and 6,324 (docs), so a local code or adherence request is never admitted single pass and is always handled in parts (trigger 'fit'), and a docs request is admitted single pass only if its evidence fits in 3,916 bytes. For a part the largest prompt plus the 4,000-byte minimum room is 15,040 bytes, within 22,528 with 7,488 spare. This departs from the wording of ac4 for local code and adherence requests; the user accepted it on 2026-11-08 (accuracy over cost), and ac4 still guarantees that a small request whose input is admitted is returned whole. If the fixed context plus the minimum room does not fit the part budget, HandlingBudgetError names the configuration (raise the window or lower PART_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS). On a local model a part reply that outgrows the cap is cut by the provider, fails validation and is handled by the repair and division rules. With no declared limit: 60,000 characters (source 'default', also used by the step tool, which has no provider). The helper owns the repair loop: it calls completeStructured with {maxAttempts: 1, internalRetry: false} (internalRetry is an existing completion option), because maxAttempts alone is ignored by CliProvider's Vibe path and the Claude and Codex paths keep transient retries; with both set no provider retries on its own. It builds each repair prompt itself with the repair note capped at 8,000 characters of listed errors (the rest counted) and applies the rule to every attempt before it is sent. Repair exhaustion has one rule everywhere: a repair that is not admitted divides the part further, up to three times; after that the part is recorded as not covered and processing continues, so a successful part is never discarded. The input is divided when the table says partitioned OR the rule does not admit it.

dataModelChanges.entity: PartPlan, PartResult and the caller adapters
dataModelChanges.details: A PartPlan is the ordered blocks of the evidence with an ordinal separate from the block key, grouped by directory then file in stable order. A block larger than the room is cut into consecutive sections, each the largest whole UTF-8 code-point prefix of the remainder that fits the room, so no code point is split and a section may leave up to three unused bytes; sections do not overlap; a section is short only if it is the final one or ends at a code-point boundary before the room is full; the 4,000-unit minimum applies to the room itself, and a room under it is a HandlingBudgetError. A PartResult holds the part's heading, its summary (capped at 2,000 characters by the schema) and its assembled content. The bundle adapter takes system, focus and summary from the final combine and concatenates structure, surface, artefacts and upstream of the covered parts by ordinal under part headings; the aggregate adapter takes the summary from the final combine and concatenates the findings of the covered parts by ordinal, each keeping its sources. A combine reply is never read for evidence or findings. Combine stages: N summaries become ceil(N/g) with g at least 2, so it ends in at most ceil(log2 N) stages. If a combine fails or is not admitted and at least one part is covered, the adapter's output is built from the per-part results with 'combine' in notCovered and nothing is thrown.

dataModelChanges.entity: HandlingBudgetError, the every-part-failed case and LookupFailedError
dataModelChanges.details: HandlingBudgetError extends ShaperAnswerStepFailedError, with a new reason 'input-does-not-fit' added to AnswerStepFailureReason (additive; the class is declared by Story s1). Every part failure is classified by cause when it happens, not by whether the call threw: 'call-failed' when isModelCallFailure(err) (src/analyze/context/model-failure.ts, the test runAggregator's classifyError already uses), 'invalid-reply' for ModelResponseShapeError, SynthesizerSchemaUnrecoverable or any other validation failure that completeStructured throws (the Ollama and Vibe providers throw after a single attempt when validation fails, and Codex throws ModelResponseShapeError), and 'unadmittable' when the rendered input is not admitted. Terminal precedence when no part is covered: HandlingBudgetError only when every uncovered part is unadmittable (or the fixed context leaves no room for a section); otherwise a ShaperAnswerStepFailedError with reason 'model-failed' if any part is 'call-failed', else 'invalid-answer', with every part's own reason in notCovered. The daemon's mapping (analyze-rpc.ts) and the plan tree's mapping (orchestrator/driver.ts), which test instanceof ShaperAnswerStepFailedError, carry the found results and report with no new branch, and the driver passes the error through unchanged. LookupFailedError (message, partial, cause) gains two optional fields: handling and answerStepReason (the original reason). The free-form lookup catches every ShaperAnswerStepFailedError from the tool loop and throws a LookupFailedError carrying the tool results as partial, the handling and the reason; failedOutput copies the reason into the failed output's errorCode as 'answer-step:<reason>' and keeps the cause, and the pipeline rebuilds the ShaperAnswerStepFailedError from that reason and the found results, so the three reasons are told apart and executePlan keeps the partial results and the report instead of attempting a second synthesis.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: AnswerStepFailureReason adds 'input-does-not-fit'; LookupFailedError adds readonly handling?: HandlingReport | undefined and readonly answerStepReason?: AnswerStepFailureReason | undefined

dataModelChanges.entity: TaskExecutionRecord.data, RunFailure.data and the failed nested plan
dataModelChanges.details: executeLeafTask(task: PlannedTask, intent, runId, outputs: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly UpstreamOutput[]>, absentInputs?, execution?) currently catches an error from the aggregate task and records the failed task with its message only, and the orchestrator turns a failed aggregate task into the run failure with the code 'executor-aggregator-failed' and a message of task counts and failure strings. TaskExecutionRecord gains an optional data field kept for any aggregate failure, built by failureData(err) as a JSON-safe value, because task and run records are written with JSON.stringify (atomicWriteJson in executor/cache.ts and orchestrator/persistence.ts), which turns an Error object into {}: for a ShaperAnswerStepFailedError (HandlingBudgetError included) { kind:'answer-step', reason, found, handling }; for a plain Error { kind:'error', name, message, cause? } with the cause nested at most 3 levels and no Error objects, functions or cycles. The original error is preserved at the classification boundary: runAggregator's classifyError builds the same prefixed Error as today but with the original error as its cause (it discarded it before), and a typed answer-step error thrown by the helper is not passed through classifyError, so executeLeafTask receives the original in both cases. The orchestrator copies it into RunFailure.data under the unchanged code when the root aggregate fails. For a nested plan, executePlannerTask marks the parent planner task failed when its child has no final report and keeps childResult, and collectPlanSources checks failure status before recursing, so a failed nested aggregate was unreachable and a root aggregate that succeeds from sibling outputs raised no run failure. The design makes collectPlanSources read the kept child records of a failed planner-kind task and add sources for the child's aggregate failure and uncovered parts, and concludeRun merge the nested handling with the root's, so the run is incomplete and names the nested failure whether or not the root aggregate succeeded.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: TaskExecutionRecord adds readonly data?: unknown (JSON-safe: AggregateFailureData)

dataModelChanges.details: AnswerProgress is {mode: 'single' | 'partitioned', trigger?: 'size' | 'fit' | 'both', plan: PartPlan (the blocks with ordinals and section cuts), budgets: HandlingReport['budgets'], completed: PartResult[] by ordinal, pending: {kind 'part' | 'combine', ordinal or stage and group index}, stageOutputs, failures: {part, reason}[], retries}. Carrying the plan, the decision and the budgets lets the progress overload of finalizeSynthesize decide whether another part remains and return the HandlingReport without recomputing from the evidence. startAnswerProgress(args, size) makes the initial value: prepareAnswerTurn calls it when the plan phase hands over, from the table and the admission of the rendered input, and the state carries it from then on; a state without progress is a legacy state and is read as single pass. The bundle handler persists progress by re-encoding the state token on every valid transition. An invalid reply increments retries, is persisted, and the current turn is re-emitted with the same prompt and a new state token and a retry note, as StepOutputEmitBundle, StepOutputEmitPart or StepOutputEmitCombine, which gain an optional retry field {attempt, reason}; it is not an error output. At the retry bound the part or the combine is recorded as failed and the flow continues; retries reset to zero when a turn advances; progress is released on terminal success and failure.

Two outputs added to the StepOutput union beside StepOutputEmitBundle with the same fields plus the part ordinal and total, or the stage and group, and the optional retry field. A reply reuses the registered bundle argument of seven string layers (a part reply is a seven-layer bundle of that part with its summary within the cap; a combine reply fills system, focus and summary and leaves the four evidence layers empty), so the registered MCP schema and StepInputBundle are unchanged and the legacy emit_bundle turn is kept. A typed answer failure is returned as StepOutputError with the declared code and its data, not as an uncaught exception.

Carries the HandlingReport of the aggregator call, validated by parseHandling on read. collectPlanSources reads it for the aggregate task of the root plan and of each nested plan, and concludeRun merges them with the run context's handling through mergeHandling, so uncovered parts make the run's completeness false.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Types HandlingReport with additive fields (combineStages, budgets in their own units, optional trigger, and 'mixed' for partitionedBy), states the composition rules, and fills it on every answer of both paths.

Fills AnswerReport.handling through applyHandling (which also adds the uncovered parts as incomplete source notes and sets complete false); keeps the binary mergeAnswerReports(first, second, prefix); renders one handling line in renderReportHead; the driver passes the updated report to the stamp callback that sets the delivered bundle's report.
A result whose part or combine failed is incomplete; plan-task completeness records are read as today and the aggregate's handling, at any depth, is added as sources.
Reads RequestMeasure.size for HANDLING_TABLE (an undetermined measure is XL) on every path; measure.characters stays a hint.

Uses the answer-step-failed code declared by sc6 and raised by Story s1 through the existing ShaperAnswerStepFailedError mappings and keeps the existing 'executor-aggregator-failed' code with data for the aggregate task; no new code.

errorCases.scenario: A part's model call fails, or its reply fails the schema after the helper's bounded repair attempts
errorCases.detection: The single-attempt call (internalRetry false) throws, or the reply fails validation and the helper's own repair count reaches the structured-output retry setting
errorCases.response: The part is recorded in failures and named in HandlingReport.notCovered with its qualified id and reason; the other parts are kept; completeness is false
errorCases.userImpact: The answer is delivered and names the part that was not covered and why

errorCases.scenario: A provider retries on its own despite maxAttempts 1
errorCases.detection: Prevented by passing internalRetry false with maxAttempts 1; a test with the real CliProvider adapters (Vibe, Claude, Codex) counts provider attempts and fails if any makes more than one
errorCases.response: No separate response: the helper is the only code that retries, and it measures every attempt
errorCases.userImpact: No unmeasured repair note can enter a call

errorCases.scenario: No part is covered (mixed terminal failures)
errorCases.detection: failures holds every part and completed is empty; the helper records for each part a failure kind chosen by cause when it happened: 'call-failed' (isModelCallFailure(err)), 'invalid-reply' (ModelResponseShapeError, SynthesizerSchemaUnrecoverable or any other validation failure thrown by completeStructured, which the Ollama, Vibe and Codex adapters throw for a schema-invalid reply) or 'unadmittable'; it applies one precedence rule
errorCases.response: HandlingBudgetError ('input-does-not-fit') only when every uncovered part is 'unadmittable', or the fixed context leaves no room for a section; otherwise a ShaperAnswerStepFailedError with reason 'model-failed' if any part is 'call-failed', else 'invalid-answer'. Either way every part's own reason is in notCovered and the lookup results and the report are carried
errorCases.userImpact: A typed failure of the right kind that keeps what the lookups found and names what happened to each part; malformed replies are reported as 'invalid-answer' and not as a failed model call even though the adapter threw; a mix of unadmittable and failed parts is reported as the failure of the call, not as a budget problem; no empty answer is written

errorCases.scenario: The combine call fails, its reply stays invalid, or the combine itself is not admitted
errorCases.detection: The combine call throws, or its reply fails validation at the repair bound, or the admission rule does not admit fixed context plus two capped summaries, with at least one part covered
errorCases.response: The output is built from the per-part results unchanged by the adapter, its summary layer being the part summaries concatenated by ordinal, and 'combine' is added to notCovered; nothing is thrown
errorCases.userImpact: The per-part results are returned with the combine failure reported

errorCases.scenario: A combine stage does not reduce the count of summaries
errorCases.detection: The helper compares the count before and after the stage
errorCases.response: The stage is treated as a combine failure and the per-part fallback applies

errorCases.scenario: The room for a section is under the 4,000-unit minimum, or the fixed context leaves no room
errorCases.detection: Fixed rendered input plus the minimum room is not admitted against the part and combine budget (with the checked-in local configuration 22,528 bytes: window 32,768 minus PART_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 8,192 minus 2,048), or every part is unadmittable
errorCases.response: HandlingBudgetError with the results and the report, whose message names the configuration to change (raise the window or lower PART_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS); no partial answer is written
errorCases.userImpact: A typed failure that says the configured window and output size leave no room

errorCases.scenario: A part reply outgrows the 8,192-token part output cap on a local model
errorCases.detection: OllamaProvider passes maxTokens as num_predict, so the provider cuts the reply mid-JSON and it fails validation; the helper sees an invalid reply for that part. A CLI provider enforces no output cap, so this case does not arise there and is not needed: a part reply never enters a later model call
errorCases.response: The repair and division rules apply: one repair attempt that is admitted, otherwise the part is divided into smaller sections up to three times, then recorded as not covered; the other parts continue
errorCases.userImpact: A part whose findings do not fit one reply is read in smaller sections or named as not covered; nothing is silently cut

errorCases.scenario: A schema-repair attempt would not be admitted
errorCases.detection: The helper builds each repair prompt itself, from the part, the schema text and the repair note capped at 8,000 characters of listed errors (the rest counted), and applies the admission rule before the attempt
errorCases.response: One rule for every repair: the part is divided into smaller sections up to three times; after that the part is recorded as not covered and the other parts continue; HandlingBudgetError is raised only under the terminal precedence rule, so a successful part is never discarded
errorCases.userImpact: A malformed reply with many errors cannot push a call over the limit unnoticed, and cannot erase findings already gathered

errorCases.scenario: A section boundary falls inside a multi-byte character
errorCases.detection: The cutter looks for the largest whole UTF-8 code-point prefix that fits the room; for 4,999 ASCII bytes followed by a four-byte emoji in a 5,000-byte room, the emoji does not fit
errorCases.response: The section ends before the emoji and the next section begins with it; the unused bytes of the first section stay unused; decoding any section gives valid text and no byte is lost
errorCases.userImpact: Every character is read whole, in exactly one section

errorCases.scenario: The provider refuses a part as too large
errorCases.detection: InputTooLargeError from the provider, whose sizes may be undefined
errorCases.response: The part is divided into smaller sections up to three times, and then recorded as not covered
errorCases.userImpact: The part is read in full or named; nothing is silently cut

errorCases.scenario: A local model's tokenizer produces more tokens than bytes
errorCases.detection: Not possible under the stated assumption that a token covers at least one input byte; template and special tokens are covered by the 2,048 reserve, and the assumption is recorded in the report as basis 'bytes-bound'
errorCases.response: No separate response: the rule admits an input only if its byte length fits, so the window is not exceeded; a model whose special tokens exceed the reserve would need the reserve raised, one constant
errorCases.userImpact: An admitted local input cannot be silently truncated; the cost is earlier division

errorCases.scenario: A typed answer failure is thrown from inside the free-form final emit
errorCases.detection: The free-form lookup catches every ShaperAnswerStepFailedError from the tool loop (HandlingBudgetError, 'model-failed' and 'invalid-answer' alike); executePlan would otherwise turn any error that is not a ConnectionExecutionError into a failed lookup with no data
errorCases.response: It throws a LookupFailedError carrying the tool results as partial, the HandlingReport and the original reason (answerStepReason); failedOutput keeps all three, copying the reason as errorCode 'answer-step:<reason>' with the cause; the pipeline rebuilds the ShaperAnswerStepFailedError from that reason and the found results, raises the answer-step failure with the report and does not attempt a second synthesis
errorCases.userImpact: The caller receives the failure with what the search found, how far the handling got and its true reason, whatever the category of the failure

errorCases.scenario: A typed answer failure is thrown from inside synthesize
errorCases.detection: The driver's catch sees HandlingBudgetError or ShaperAnswerStepFailedError
errorCases.response: The driver passes it through unchanged instead of mapping it to 'answer-invalid'; the daemon's and the plan tree's mappings, which test instanceof ShaperAnswerStepFailedError, carry its results and report; the step tool returns it as StepOutputError with the declared code and its data
errorCases.userImpact: The caller receives the error with the lookup results and the report

errorCases.scenario: A partitioned answer succeeds in part on the ordinary lookup path (a part or the combine is not covered)
errorCases.detection: synthesizeHandled returns layers and a HandlingReport whose notCovered is non-empty; the driver calls applyHandling on found.report before returning the 'bundle' outcome
errorCases.response: applyHandling sets report.handling, adds one incomplete source note per uncovered part ('answer step / <part id>') and sets completeness.complete false; settlePipelineOutcome passes this updated report to the stamp callback, so the delivered bundle's report carries the handling, the uncovered parts and complete=false instead of the lookups' complete=true
errorCases.userImpact: A partial answer is never delivered as complete; the head names the parts that were not covered and why

errorCases.scenario: The aggregator's classifyError would discard the original error
errorCases.detection: classifyError builds a fresh prefixed Error; before this Story it passed no cause, so nothing downstream could read the original
errorCases.response: classifyError keeps the prefix and message and sets the original error as the new Error's cause; a typed ShaperAnswerStepFailedError from the helper is thrown unwrapped and is not passed to classifyError; failureData reads the cause chain
errorCases.userImpact: The run's failure data names the real cause of an aggregate failure

errorCases.scenario: A failure is thrown from inside runAggregator
errorCases.detection: executeLeafTask catches the aggregate task's error: either a ShaperAnswerStepFailedError (HandlingBudgetError included), thrown unwrapped by the helper, or a plain Error built by classifyError with an aggregator prefix and the original error as its cause, for example a single call that failed with no part results
errorCases.response: The failed record keeps the failure in its optional data field as failureData(err), a JSON-safe value: { kind:'answer-step', reason, found, handling } for a typed error, { kind:'error', name, message, cause? } for a plain Error with the cause nested at most 3 levels and no Error objects (task and run records are written with JSON.stringify, which turns an Error into {}). When the root aggregate fails the orchestrator copies it into RunFailure.data under the unchanged code 'executor-aggregator-failed'
errorCases.userImpact: A failed aggregation keeps what it carried, including the original cause message, whatever the kind of error, and survives being stored and read back; the run says how far the handling got

errorCases.scenario: A nested plan's aggregate fails while the root aggregate succeeds from sibling outputs
errorCases.detection: executePlannerTask returns a failed record with the kept childResult; collectPlanSources reads the child's records of a failed planner-kind task before it would stop at the failure status
errorCases.response: A source for the nested aggregate's failure and for each uncovered part is added with the nested task path, and concludeRun merges the nested handling with the root's, so the run is incomplete and names the nested failure although no run failure was raised
errorCases.userImpact: A run never reports complete over a nested aggregation that failed

errorCases.scenario: An invalid reply for a part or combine turn on the step tool
errorCases.detection: finalizeSynthesize (the progress overload) raises SynthesizerSchemaUnrecoverable for the current turn
errorCases.response: The bundle handler increments progress.retries, persists the progress with a new state token and re-emits the current turn with the same prompt and a retry note; the client is never stranded without a token; at the retry bound the part or the combine is recorded as failed
errorCases.userImpact: The client sees the same turn again with the reason, and the flow cannot loop for ever

errorCases.scenario: A stored handling value is malformed
errorCases.detection: parseHandling finds a missing required field or a wrong type, as for the stored {}
errorCases.response: The value is treated as absent by mergeHandling, renderReportHead and isAnswerReport; it is not written back
errorCases.userImpact: An old record is read without handling instead of failing

admission for a local model with the checked-in values (32,768 window, 20,480 single-pass output, 2,048 reserve) is 10,240 bytes for a single pass: exactly 10,240 is admitted, one byte over is divided, multi-byte text is counted in bytes; part and combine calls use PART_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 8,192 and a limit of 22,528 bytes; a window that leaves less than fixed context plus 4,000 bytes gives HandlingBudgetError naming the configuration

with the real code, adherence and docs prompts the single-pass decision for the checked-in local configuration is 'not admitted' for code (10,652 bytes) and adherence (11,040), and admitted for docs only when the evidence is at most 3,916 bytes; every part prompt plus the 4,000-byte minimum room (15,040 at most) fits 22,528
a CLI provider is admitted in characters against its declared budget minus 16,000, and the two units are never compared

the helper calls the provider with {maxAttempts: 1, internalRetry: false} and builds each repair prompt itself: the note is capped at 8,000 characters with the rest counted, every attempt is admitted before it is sent, and a fake provider that would retry internally is never allowed to

repair exhaustion has one outcome: an unadmitted repair divides the part up to three times, then the part is recorded as not covered and the others continue; a part that already succeeded is never discarded

terminal precedence when no part is covered, with failures classified by cause: every uncovered part 'unadmittable' gives HandlingBudgetError; a mix of unadmittable and 'invalid-reply' parts gives ShaperAnswerStepFailedError 'invalid-answer'; any 'call-failed' part (isModelCallFailure) gives 'model-failed'; a thrown schema-invalid error (ModelResponseShapeError, SynthesizerSchemaUnrecoverable) is 'invalid-reply', not 'call-failed'; each part's own reason is in notCovered

sections are the largest whole code-point prefix that fits the room: a 6,000-byte ASCII block in a room of 5,000 gives 5,000 and 1,000; 4,999 ASCII bytes then a four-byte emoji gives 4,999 and a second section that starts with the emoji; every section decodes to valid text, none overlaps, none is dropped; ordinals separate from keys
combine terminates: N summaries become ceil(N/g) per stage and a stage whose count does not fall is a combine failure
a combine failure, including a combine that is not admitted, with at least one part covered returns the per-part results with 'combine' in notCovered and throws nothing
the bundle adapter and the aggregate adapter keep evidence layers and findings exactly, in order, through several combine stages

alternativesConsidered.name: Size table plus an enforced input-admission rule with per-call output caps, in one shared helper that owns the repair loop, with cause-classified failures, carried-data failures and a rendered handling line
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One helper divides an answer-writing call's input when the HLD's size table says so or when the rendered input is not admitted by a provable bound, gives part and combine calls on a local model a lower stated output cap, owns the schema-repair loop with provider retries off, classifies every failure by cause, and carries the handling report and any failure's reason and data to the delivered answer on every path.
alternativesConsidered.approach: (1) Decision: partition when EITHER the measured size (sc3) is M, L or XL (undetermined is XL), OR the rendered input is not admitted. (2) Admission in two units never mixed. CLI provider: declared inputBudgetChars minus a 16,000-character reserve (characters); no output cap is enforced or needed for a CLI provider, because the CLI adapters do not enforce maxTokens (modelArgs ignores the completion options, Vibe forwards no limit) and a part reply's size never enters a later model call: the combine reads only the part summaries, capped at 2,000 characters by the schema, and the evidence layers are assembled in code from the replies into the delivered answer. Local model: the UTF-8 byte length must not exceed window tokens minus the call's output tokens minus 2,048 (bytes), because every token covers at least one byte. A single-pass call keeps the full configured output tokens (no truncation knob): with the checked-in configuration 32,768 - 20,480 - 2,048 = 10,240 bytes, and since the existing prompts alone are 10,652 (code), 11,040 (adherence) and 6,324 (docs) bytes, a local code or adherence request is never admitted single-pass and is handled in parts (trigger 'fit'); a docs request is admitted only if its evidence fits in 3,916 bytes. Part and combine calls on a local model use a stated lower output cap PART_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 8,192, enforced by OllamaProvider as num_predict: 32,768 - 8,192 - 2,048 = 22,528 bytes, which holds the largest prompt (11,040) plus the 4,000-byte minimum room (15,040) and leaves 7,488 spare. A part reply cut at 8,192 tokens ends mid-JSON, fails validation and is handled as an invalid reply by the repair and division rules. This departs from the wording of ac4 for local code and adherence requests, which the user accepted on 2026-11-08 under accuracy over cost; ac4 still guarantees that a small request whose input is admitted is returned whole. (3) The helper owns the repair loop with {maxAttempts: 1, internalRetry: false}, a repair note capped at 8,000 characters, and admission before every attempt; tests run the real adapters. (4) Failures are classified by cause when they happen: each part records a failure kind, 'call-failed' (isModelCallFailure(err) from src/analyze/context/model-failure.ts, the test aggregator.ts classifyError already uses), 'invalid-reply' (ModelResponseShapeError, SynthesizerSchemaUnrecoverable or any other validation failure thrown by completeStructured, which the Ollama, Vibe and Codex adapters throw for a schema-invalid reply) or 'unadmittable'. Terminal precedence when no part is covered: HandlingBudgetError only when every uncovered part is unadmittable; otherwise ShaperAnswerStepFailedError with 'model-failed' if any part is 'call-failed', else 'invalid-answer', with every part's own reason in notCovered. (5) Division by directory then file, sections the largest whole code-point prefix that fits the room, a room under 4,000 refused, ordinals separate from keys, part summaries capped at 2,000 characters, evidence and findings assembled in code, a staged combine of N into ceil(N/g). One repair-exhaustion rule: an unadmitted repair divides the part up to three times, then the part is recorded as not covered. A combine failure or unadmitted combine with a covered part returns the per-part results with 'combine' in notCovered. (6) Ordinary synthesis success transition: synthesizeHandled(args) returns { layers, handling } and synthesize(args) stays as a wrapper returning the layers; applyHandling(report, handling) in completeness.ts sets report.handling by mergeHandling, adds one incomplete source note per not-covered part and sets complete false when a part is not covered; the context driver builds found' with that report and returns it in the 'bundle' outcome, so settlePipelineOutcome hands the updated report to the stamp callback that sets the delivered bundle's report. (7) Callers and failure routes: LookupFailedError carries partial, handling and the original reason (answerStepReason); failedOutput copies the reason as errorCode 'answer-step:<reason>' and keeps the cause, and the pipeline rebuilds the ShaperAnswerStepFailedError from reason and found. runAggregator's classifyError keeps the original error as the cause of the prefixed Error (prefixes unchanged) and leaves a typed answer-step error unwrapped. executeLeafTask(task: PlannedTask, intent, runId, outputs: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly UpstreamOutput[]>, absentInputs?, execution?): Promise<TaskExecutionRecord> keeps failure data for any aggregate failure in the optional data field of TaskExecutionRecord as a JSON-safe value built by failureData(err): { kind:'answer-step', reason, found, handling } for a typed error, { kind:'error', name, message, cause? } for a plain Error with the cause nested at most 3 levels and no Error objects or functions, because records are written with JSON.stringify; the orchestrator puts it in RunFailure.data under 'executor-aggregator-failed'. For a failed nested plan, collectPlanSources reads the kept child records and concludeRun merges nested handling even when the root aggregate succeeded. (8) Reporting: HandlingReport with budgets in their own units, optional trigger, mergeHandling, parseHandling, renderReportHead line. (9) Step tool: AnswerProgress carries the partition plan (blocks with ordinals and section cuts), the handling decision (mode and trigger) and the measured budgets as well as the completed parts, the cursor, stage outputs, failures and retries, so the progress overload of finalizeSynthesize can decide whether another part remains and return the HandlingReport; startAnswerProgress creates it; an invalid reply re-emits the turn with a new token and a retry note.
pros: Keeps the HLD's table and an admission bound that works with the checked-in prompts and configuration
Part and combine calls fit the largest existing prompt with room to spare, and the output cap is stated only where it is enforced
Failures keep their true cause, reason and data through the free-form executor, the aggregator boundary, the walker, the persisted record, the orchestrator, nested plans and the daemon
The delivered bundle's report carries the handling and the uncovered parts on the ordinary success path
Progress is self-sufficient for the finalizer

alternativesConsidered.name: Size table only, separate implementations per path
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Decide only from the five sizes with a fixed table and implement division and combine once for the lookup pipeline and once for the aggregator.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Define a table from size to single pass or partitioned with fixed part counts, and implement the division and combine separately for synthesize and for runAggregator. The size class decides; there is no check that a call is admitted.
pros: Follows the HLD wording of a stated table literally
Each path can be tuned independently
cons: A size class counts files and items, not characters, so a medium request with large items can still overflow a call
Two implementations that can drift apart
Fixed part counts do not follow the model in use
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Literal to the HLD but a size class does not bound what a model accepts.

alternativesConsidered.name: Smallest: halve and retry when the provider refuses the input
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep one pass as today and only when the provider refuses the input as too large split it in half, retry and combine the halves.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Catch the provider's size refusal in synthesize and runAggregator, split the input at a file boundary into two halves, run each and combine, repeating on refusal. No table, no budget, no step tool part turn beyond a retry.
cons: Only the CLI provider refuses; a local model truncates silently, so input is lost with no signal, which defeats accuracy
The sizes in a refusal may be absent so the split point is a guess
No section rule for one large item and no handling report, so ac3 and ac6 are not met by design
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: A local model truncates silently instead of refusing, so input is lost with no signal; this violates k1, k2 and k3.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: How a step-tool answer is handled in parts: the handler creates the initial progress, the helper decides, the client replies per part, progress is persisted on every transition, an invalid reply re-emits the turn with a new token, and the combine ends with the assembled answer or the per-part fallback.

participants.label: Step handler
participants.description: Creates the initial progress, validates each reply and persists the progress by re-encoding the state token.

participants.label: Handling helper
participants.description: Applies the table and the admission rule, divides the evidence, assembles output in code.

messages.label: startAnswerProgress(args, size)
messages.description: Creates the initial progress: single or partitioned.

messages.label: prepareSynthesize(args, progress)
messages.description: Asks for the next turn: answer, part or combine.

messages.label: turn that is admitted
messages.description: The rendered input of the turn passes the admission rule.

messages.label: emit_part / emit_combine
messages.description: The prompt, user turn and schema of the turn, with the new state token.

messages.label: bundle reply
messages.description: A seven-layer reply for the part, or system, focus and summary for a combine.

messages.label: finalizeSynthesize(reply, execution, progress)
messages.description: The progress overload: a bad reply increments retries and the same turn is re-emitted with a new token and a retry note; at the bound the part or the combine is recorded as failed.

messages.label: next progress or final bundle
messages.description: Evidence and findings are assembled in code; a combine failure returns the per-part results.
